articles.title: Indian Navy rescues 20 crew from fishing vessel hijacked off Somalia - The News Mill
articles.content: ANI Photo | Indian Navy rescues 20 crew from fishing vessel hijacked off Somalia The Indian Navy successfully rescued all 20 crew members of the fishing vessel Azini after it was hijacked by armed pirates off the northeastern coast of Somalia last month. The operation, which lasted over 48 hours, concluded without any casualties or injuries. The hijacking posed a significant maritime security threat, as the vessel risked being used as a ‘mother ship’ for launching further pirate attacks against merchant shipping in the region. In response, the Indian Navy deployed a warship supported by a maritime reconnaissance aircraft to locate and track the vessel. Persistent surveillance allowed the Navy to contain the vessel’s movement and prevent its escape using calibrated non-kinetic measures. The Indian Navy then carried out a swift and coordinated tactical intervention to secure the vessel, neutralise the pirate threat, and ensure the safe release of all crew members. In a statement, the Indian Navy said, “The successful operation is a testament to the Indian Navy’s high operational preparedness and ability to undertake complex maritime security operations through seamless inter-service coordination. It also underscores India’s unwavering commitment to remaining First Responder and Preferred Security Partner in the Indian Ocean Region.” ADVERTISEMENT The Navy reaffirmed its dedication to safeguarding seafarers, protecting vital maritime trade routes, and maintaining a secure and stable maritime environment in the Indian Ocean Region. articles.title: Phase 2 of India's First Digital Census to Begin on Jan 10 - Pragativadi
articles.content: I ndia is set to roll out the second phase of its landmark Census 2026 starting January 10, marking a major milestone as the country conducts its first-ever fully digital population count. Under the Phase 2 roadmap, citizens will have a 15-day window to log into an official portal or mobile application to fill in their demographic details directly through self-enumeration. Following this initial digital drive, enumerators will carry out door-to-door visits from January 25 to February 28 to gather information from households across the nation. This comprehensive phase features 40 detailed questions covering crucial socioeconomic indicators, including education levels, healthcare access, employment status, and caste details. Staff training programs will continue through December to ensure smooth execution, with the central government targeting complete data collection by April. The digital-first framework aims to streamline data entry, minimise errors, and significantly reduce processing timelines for national demographic records. articles.title: Explained: India's First Hydrogen - Powered Train Advances Green Rail Mobility
articles.content: Indian Railways is entering a new era of clean and sustainable transportation. Hydrogen fuel cell technology has emerged globally as a promising alternative to fossil fuel-based traction systems. India's first indigenous hydrogen-powered train marks an important step in adopting this next-generation technology. It is a locomotive that generates its own electricity onboard using hydrogen. With the inauguration on 17 July 2026 , the hydrogen fuel cell-powered train is set to begin operations. It will run on the Jind-Sonipat section of the Northern Railway. The project combines advanced propulsion technology with dedicated hydrogen storage, refuelling and operational infrastructure. It will demonstrate the feasibility of clean rail transportation in India. Developed as a pilot initiative, the project reflects Indian Railways' commitment to innovation. It also advances energy efficiency and environmentally responsible transportation. With this, India joins a select group of countries exploring hydrogen-powered rail transportation. These include Germany, Japan, China and the United States. As the technology remains at a nascent stage, the project will provide valuable operational experience. This will support future applications of hydrogen-powered mobility in the railway sector. Inside India's First Hydrogen Train The hydrogen train project has been developed in accordance with design approval and technical specifications prepared by the Research, Design & Standards Organisation (RDSO) . Designed and developed entirely in India, the project demonstrates the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat . Technology Behind the Train Hydrogen fuel cell technology produces electricity through a chemical reaction using hydrogen. The primary energy source is a Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) . This is a fuel cell that generates electricity by reacting hydrogen and oxygen across a proton-conducting Perfluorosulfonic Acid (PFSA) polymer membrane. The process produces only water vapour and heat as byproducts. Hydrogen is a high-energy fuel, 120 MJ/Kg (megajoules per kilogram) in comparison to diesel, which is 43 MJ/Kg. It is low maintenance with a manageable carbon footprint. This makes hydrogen the cleanest propulsion technology currently available for rail transport. To support this, Indian Railways has established dedicated infrastructure. The country's largest railway hydrogen storage and refuelling facility has been established at Jind, Haryana . The indigenous facility stores nearly 3,000 kg of hydrogen at a time. It will support hydrogen-powered train operations. The Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO) has granted the required licence. The licence covers storage and dispensing of compressed hydrogen gas at the site. The hydrogen ecosystem has been designed in accordance with internationally accepted standards. This includes NFPA-2 (National Fire Protection Association) and ISO (International Organisation for Standardisation) 19880 Series. The entire system underwent an independent third-party safety assessment. It was done by TÜV SÜD, Germany, one of the world's leading technical inspection and certification agencies. The train consists of two Hydrogen Driving Power Cars (DPCs) and eight Trailer Coaches (TCs) . Each DPC houses fuel cells, lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries and hydrogen storage cylinders. articles.title: KSLTA becomes India's first state tennis body to adopt National Sports Governance Act, 2025
articles.content: KSLTA becomes India's first state tennis body to adopt National Sports Governance Act, 2025 IANS November 2, 2026 6:01 PM Share on | Bengaluru, Nov 2 (IANS) In a landmark move for sports administration in the country, the Karnataka State Lawn Tennis Association (KSLTA) has become the first state tennis association in India to adopt the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, following a unanimous resolution at its Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM) held in Bengaluru. The resolution was adopted unanimously following active participation and deliberations by members representing the association, reflecting a collective commitment to embracing the principles of transparency, accountability, ethical administration and good governance envisaged under the new legislation. The National Sports Governance Act, 2025, enacted by the Government of India, seeks to establish a robust and transparent framework for the administration of sports in the country. It emphasises institutional accountability, democratic functioning, athlete welfare, ethical practices and effective grievance-redressal mechanisms, while seeking to bring Indian sports administration in line with international best practices. The move by KSLTA follows the All India Tennis Association's (AITA) adoption of amendments to its Constitution on July 26, 2026, to bring it in conformity with the new legislation, making it one of the first National Sports Federations in the country to align with the Act. With the unanimous decision, KSLTA has now taken the lead among state tennis associations in embracing the new governance framework, setting an important precedent for other state associations across the country. Maheshwar Rao, IAS, Chief Commissioner of Greater Bengaluru Authority and also Secy KSLTA said, "Sports in India is at an important crossroads, and the National Sports Policy 2025 provides us with a comprehensive roadmap for the future. We believe that the responsibility of taking this vision forward does not rest with the government alone. Sports associations have an equally important role to play in translating these objectives into meaningful action on the ground. Sunil Yajaman, Jt. Secy, AITA and also Jt. Secy, KSLTA said, "While AITA has already taken the lead at the national federation level, we are proud that KSLTA is the first state tennis association in the country to adopt this framework. We hope this initiative inspires other state associations to embrace these reforms and collectively contribute towards building a stronger sporting ecosystem in India." --IANS hs/
